rationale: Framed as a considered-and-cleared question that asserts no defect; and the rewrite (CASE WHEN c.Name IS NOT NULL THEN c.Name -> c.Name) removes a wrapper that was itself non-sargable, so if anything sargability improves.

The asymmetry is real: Equals compares IList values element-wise (lines 99-126) while GetHashCode hashes Value directly (line 130), so the new HashSet<SqlExpression> at SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:580 could miss structurally equal list constants. Pre-existing and practically unreachable here, since an IS NOT NULL operand is essentially never a list-valued constant.

A real gap remains: no added test produces an AndAlso where only the right conjunct drops, or where binary.Update rebuilds with a changed child (three conjuncts with a middle drop). Partly overstated though — Is_not_null_optimizes_binary_op_with_mixed_checks does exercise the 'left is null ? right' arm.
Same substance as the human naming thread: a void accumulator named with a noun phrase; the thread proposes DetectNullPropagatingNodes.

Factually right that negative1/2 guard on LeaderNickname while the result uses a different column/entity, but that is their purpose — they are negative cases pinning that the optimization must not fire, and their SQL is correctly unchanged. No defect asserted and no action follows.

The rewritten test is indeed not re-Visited, but dropping IS NOT NULL conjuncts from an AndAlso chain cannot make a surviving conjunct trivially true or false — the survivors are untouched, already-simplified subtrees, and binary.Update returns the same node when children are unchanged. The asserted consequence is not demonstrable.

True by construction: returning clause.Result unguarded means the THEN expression is now evaluated on rows the CASE previously short-circuited, so an expensive result (UDF, scalar subquery) runs for every row. Real trade-off but speculative in magnitude, and the guard removal is the point of the change.

Asking for a test that pins the absence of an optimization the TODO explicitly defers; such a baseline test would only have to be deleted when the TODO is done, and the shape's correctness is already covered elsewhere.

Correct and actionable: operands.Add's bool result is discarded and recursion is unconditional, so a shared subexpression is re-walked on every path reaching it; guarding with 'if (!operands.Add(expression)) return;' fixes it. Impact is bounded by expression-tree size.

The file has an established relational-nulls convention (CreateContext(useRelationalNulls: true) used ~20 times), and the new CASE rewrite still fires under that mode, so a variant would be consistent. Small, and I did not verify that the emitted SQL actually differs there.

Same substance as the human thread naming AtTimeZone and Collate: expression types the processor visits are not SqlBinaryExpression/SqlUnaryExpression/SqlFunctionExpression, so they fall through the null-propagation model and the optimization silently misses them.

Genuine gap: every added test exercises propagating arguments only, so nothing pins that a false entry in ArgumentsPropagateNullability keeps the IS NOT NULL check. Given the analysis is what licenses dropping a guard, a negative test there has real value.

ProcessNullNotNull (line 2242 onward) already encodes the same null-propagation model — unary Convert/Not/Negate, binary except AndAlso/OrElse, function instance/argument propagation, plus a COALESCE special case — and the new local copy has drifted from it. That is the human thread's point that this should be general shared machinery rather than a local case utility.
Same substance as the human nit that the if/else-if type-pattern chain would read better as one switch with pattern matching.
A considered-and-cleared conformance check: the new tests do use [ConditionalTheory]/[MemberData(nameof(IsAsyncData))] and neighbor naming, so no defect is asserted.

Factually accurate: the test is visited with preserveColumnNullabilityInformation: true, so clause.Result at line 534 was simplified with the test's columns in _nonNullableColumns, and the new rewrite then deletes the guard that justified that assumption. Substantive interaction nobody raised; I could not construct a concrete miscompilation, since the drop also requires the simplified result to propagate null from the same operand — hence the low confidence.

Asking a query-optimization PR to add a compilation benchmark fixture is out of proportion; the change's effect is on emitted SQL, which the added SQL baselines already pin, and EF Core does not gate such PRs on benchmark coverage.
